slides.title: Unique ID Generator Overview
content: A unique ID generator produces globally unique identifiers across distributed systems
Ensures no collisions even when multiple machines generate IDs simultaneously
Often designed to be time-sortable for better database indexing
Used in large-scale distributed applications
Focuses on performance, scalability, and uniqueness

slides.title: Key Requirements
content: IDs must be globally unique across all nodes
Should be time-ordered or sortable
Must fit within 64-bit constraints
Should be numeric for efficiency
Must support high throughput and low latency
Should scale across distributed systems

slides.title: Auto Increment IDs
content: Database automatically increments ID for each new record
Provides simple and sequential ID generation
Ensures natural ordering of IDs
Cannot scale across distributed systems
Creates a single point of failure and bottleneck

slides.title: Multi Master Auto Increment
content: Multiple database servers generate IDs using offset and step logic
Each server generates IDs independently
Avoids central coordination
Difficult to manage when adding or removing servers
Can waste ID space and complicate scaling

slides.title: UUID Approach
content: UUID generates 128-bit random unique identifiers
Does not require coordination between nodes
Extremely low probability of collision
Not time sortable which affects indexing
Large size impacts storage and performance

slides.title: Ticket Server Approach
content: Centralized service generates sequential IDs
Clients request ID from the server
Ensures strict ordering of IDs
Becomes a bottleneck under high load
Introduces network latency and single point of failure

slides.title: Snowflake ID Overview
content: Snowflake is a distributed ID generation algorithm
Generates 64-bit unique IDs without central coordination
Combines timestamp, machine ID, and sequence number
Provides time-ordered IDs
Highly scalable and efficient for distributed systems

slides.title: Snowflake Structure
content: 1 bit reserved for sign
41 bits used for timestamp in milliseconds
10 bits used for machine identifier
12 bits used for sequence number
Structure ensures uniqueness and ordering

slides.title: Snowflake Generation Process
content: System gets current timestamp in milliseconds
If same timestamp, sequence number is incremented
If sequence exceeds limit, system waits for next millisecond
Combines timestamp, machine ID, and sequence
Returns a unique 64-bit ID

slides.title: Snowflake Advantages
content: Generates globally unique IDs
Ensures time ordering for better indexing
Scales horizontally without coordination
No central bottleneck
Supports millions of IDs per second

slides.title: Snowflake Limitations
content: Depends on system clock accuracy
Clock drift can cause incorrect ordering
Requires proper machine ID assignment
Slightly complex implementation compared to simple methods
Needs monitoring for time synchronization

slides.title: Clock Synchronization Issue
content: Occurs when system clock moves backward
May cause duplicate or out-of-order IDs
System can block ID generation temporarily
Logical timestamps can be used as alternative
Requests may be rejected until clock stabilizes

slides.title: Comparison of Approaches
content: Auto increment is simple but not scalable
Multi-master provides distribution but complex management
UUID ensures uniqueness but not ordering
Ticket server ensures order but creates bottleneck
Snowflake balances scalability, ordering, and performance

slides.title: Core Concepts
content: Distributed systems operate across multiple machines
Uniqueness ensures no duplicate IDs
Sortable IDs improve database performance
Scalability allows handling increasing load
Horizontal scaling adds more machines instead of upgrading one

slides.title: Important Terms
content: Bottleneck is a component limiting system performance
Single point of failure is a component whose failure stops system
Epoch is a custom starting time for timestamps
Machine ID uniquely identifies each server
Sequence number generates multiple IDs in same time unit
Monotonicity ensures IDs always increase

slides.title: Final Summary
content: Unique ID generation is critical in distributed systems
Different approaches provide trade-offs in scalability and ordering
Snowflake is the most balanced and widely used solution
Combines timestamp, machine ID, and sequence number
Provides scalable, unique, and time-ordered IDs efficiently
